scenes.title: C major
scenes.subtitle: The classic stretch.
lines: This lesson teaches the classic stretch — the C major chord.
It's a key shape in changing chords, and we'll learn it step by step.

scenes.heading: C major (C)
lines: Place finger 3 on string 5 at fret 3, finger 2 on string 4 at fret 2, and finger 1 on string 2 at fret 1.
Don't play string 6 — start your strum on string 5.
The stretch may feel hard at first, but that's normal.
Keep your thumb low behind the neck and practise slowly.
Let's learn the C major chord — a friendly shape that sounds great in many songs.
Here's how it sounds: strummed, then string by string.
scenes.tip: Skip string 6. Finger 2 has to arch over string 3 so the open G rings.

lines: Let's practice changing between C major and G major.
Move your fingers smoothly from one shape to the next, and you'll start to feel how these chords fit together.
Place your fingers, strum from the fifth string, and let's play.
The app is listening — take a breath, and play your first C major chord.
